headline: Technical Artist
intro: I sit between art and code: shaders, modular assets, animation and particle work, and the in-editor tooling that lets a small team produce a lot without repeating itself. These are the projects where the art pipeline was the interesting problem.

bullets: Authored a toon shader with an outline pass
Built the game's full UI on a one-week jam schedule
Delivered the art-facing systems alongside dialogue and quest tooling
Created all 3D animations and particle effects
Modelled the station interior and exterior set dressing
Built a dialogue system that stays in sync with recorded voice acting
Modelled 3D assets and built 2D UI tools so the interface reads as part of the world
Integrated UI and the 3D main-menu scene into a single space
Produced the environment art for two distinct worlds in two weeks
Built particle systems and animations for the 3D assets
Kept the world low-poly to hold performance in a web build
Engineered a modular first-person gun system shared across weapon types
Wrote a Unity Shader Graph shader that randomises car colours, reusing one material instead of many
Built a spawner that ramps difficulty over the course of a run
Produced all pixel art as modular, reusable pieces
Implemented chunked map loading to keep performance stable
Built a modular wave system so new objectives could be authored quickly
